content:
The Cabinet
Member for Parks, Highways & Transport Services has given
approval to the following recommendations:

(1) 
To continue with the previous decision made on 22nd October 2024 to
proceed with the Bus Pinch Points – Compstall Road Zebra
Crossing scheme, with the inclusion of an additional disabled
parking bay on Cote Green Lane, as shown on Drawing F-0700 007-10
Rev B within Appendix E.


(2) 
That approval be given to the amended TROs associated with the Bus
Pinch Points – Compstall Road Zebra Crossing scheme and that
the orders be made as set out within the revised schedule which was
included as Appendix A to the report submitted to the Marple Area
Committee on 11th March 2026.
A public question
from a resident was submitted in relation to the proposed Zebra
Crossing at the Marple Area Committee on 11th March 2026. The
details of the question and associated response included within the
minutes from the meeting, copy of the Stage 1 Road Safety Audit and
associated Designer’s Response and the drawing of the
Visibility Splays were considered by the Cabinet Member in making
the decision to approve the scheme. These are included as
Appendices A-C to this decision record.

given approval to the following small-scale highway measures within
the vicinity of Cheadle Primary School to support the existing

Approval of policies under The Renters Rights

content:
The Committee has
considered a report detailing a package of proposed Housing
Authority Enforcement Policies and has given approval to:-
 
(1) The Housing
Authority Enforcement Policy (Appendix 1), which includes:
 

·        
Statement of principles to determine penalty charges under Smoke
and CO Regulations

·        
Statement of Principles to determine penalty charge for a breach of
Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards (MEES).
 
(2) The accompanying
standalone policy relating to the how financial penalties are
calculated and issued in relation to private sector housing
offences and lettings breaches as follows:
 

·        
Civil Penalties under the Renters’ Rights Act and other
housing legislation (Appendix 2).
 
(3) Pursuant to
paragraph 1.4 of the Cabinet Procedure Rules, the amendment and
updating of the council’s scheme of delegation, to allow the
Director of Place Management to authorise officers to use the new
powers and duties in the Act and associated legislation which the
Act amends, as necessary and if required.
 
(4) Modifications and
updates to the policy, such as those in response to changes to
legislation and new statutory requirements, in consultation with
the Cabinet Member for Housing & Environment.

Do nothing - This
option is not recommended because this option would prevent the
Council from enforcing its statutory duties under the Renters
Rights Act 2025.

None.

purpose:
The Customer Feedback Annual Report 2025/26
outlines how Stockport Homes Group (SHG) uses customer feedback to
improve services, meet Housing Ombudsman requirements, and place
customer insight at the heart of service delivery.
content:
The Chair and Cabinet
Member for Housing & Environment (Councillor Jake Austin)
submitted a report (copies of which had been circulated) providing
assurance to the Council in respect of the commitment of Stockport
Homes Group to listening to customer feedback and providing high
quality services.
 
The Chair reported
that the annual report provided an overview of customer feedback,
trends, improvements made and areas for continued development.
 
The following comments
were made/ issues raised:-
 

·        
The Committee welcomed the report and noted that it had been well
received by the Housing, Economy & Environment Scrutiny
Committee.

·        
It was stated that Stockport Homes had strong overall
complaint-handling performance and high levels of compliance with
the Housing Ombudsman’s requirements.

·        
The Committee noted evidence of learning from complaints and
welcomed the role residents played in shaping complaint handling
and service improvement through customer complaint panels.

·        
It was reported that there had been investment in customer insight,
including expansion of the feedback team and targeted improvements
in areas such as repairs and maintenance.

·        
The Committee welcomed the focus on reaching customers whose voices
were less often heard, including through the “Finding
Silence” initiative.

·        
The increase in feedback received via Members of Parliament and
councillors was discussed. It was noted that scrutiny members had
considered possible reasons for this increase and that some
councillors had reported, anecdotally, a recent reduction in
residents needing to escalate matters through elected
representatives.

·        
The Committee discussed the impact of artificial intelligence on
complaints. It was reported that Stockport Homes was seeing an
increase in AI-supported complaints, which could assist residents
who may face barriers in writing complaints but could also create
challenges where correspondence was lengthy, unclear or based on
inaccurate information.

·        
It was noted that Stockport Homes sought to engage directly with
residents, including by telephone or other routes, to understand
the underlying issue and resolve complaints rather than becoming
engaged in lengthy correspondence that did not address the
substance of the matter.

·        
It was further noted that the use of AI in complaints was likely to
develop and would need to be monitored both by Stockport Homes and
more widely across the Council.
 
RESOLVED – That
the report be noted.

purpose:
This report sets out the context,
considerations and rationale for the allocation of the Crisis and
Resilience Fund (CRF).
content:
The Cabinet has
considered a report setting out the context, considerations and
rationale for the proposed Crisis and Resilience Fund (CRF)
delivery programme covering the financial years 2026/27 to 2028/29
and has:-
 
(1) Approved the
proposed approach to the delivery of the Crisis and Resilience Fund
(CRF) for the period 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2029, including:
 

·        
The overall delivery framework, incorporating the four CRF strands
of Crisis Payments, Housing Payments, Resilience Services and
Community Coordination;

·        
The strategic principles set out in this report, including a focus
on prevention, financial resilience and a “no wrong
door” approach to support;

·        
The proposed allocation approach and priorities for investment
across the programme; and

·        
The alignment of CRF delivery with the Council’s wider
priorities, including Live Well.
 
(2) Delegated
authority to the Executive Director for Corporate and Support
Services, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Finance,
Resources & Innovation to undertake the following:
 

·        
Finalise the detailed design and implementation of the
Council’s Crisis and Resilience Fund (CRF) delivery model, in
line with the principles set out in this report and the
requirements of the grant determination;

·        
Allocate funding across the approved CRF delivery strands, ensuring
alignment with local priorities and emerging needs;

·        
Commission, procure and award contracts, grants or service
agreements necessary to deliver the CRF programme, in accordance
with the Council’s Contract Procedure Rules and relevant
legislation; and

·        
Make adjustments to funding
allocations and delivery approaches, including the reallocation of
resources between schemes or priorities, to respond to demand,
performance or emerging pressures.
 
(3) Delegated to the
Chief Governance Officer and Monitoring Officer authority to
negotiate, finalise and enter into all necessary agreements and
contracts to give effect to the decisions contained in this
report.

The option of not
delivering the Crisis & Resilience Fund has been considered and
discounted.
 
Acceptance of the
funding enables the Council to provide essential support to
residents experiencing financial hardship and to deliver
preventative interventions that reduce demand on statutory
services. Failure to implement the programme would result in lost
external funding, increased pressure on frontline services, and a
reduced ability to support vulnerable households, which would be
contrary to the Council’s strategic priorities, including its
Fair & Inclusive ambition and wider prevention agenda

None.

purpose:
An initial consultation on a proposal to
amalgamate Nevill Road Infant School and Nevill Road Junior School
was held between 21 January and 24 February 2026. The Director of
Education, Skills and Work considered the outcome of the
consultation and with delegated powers, took the decision to
publish statutory proposals on 9 March 2026. The representation
period on the statutory proposals ended on 28 April 2026. Statutory
timescales are clear that a decision on proposals must take place
within two months following the closure of the period of
representation. This report considers the representations submitted
and the information contained within the statutory proposals and
makes recommendations.
content:
The Cabinet has
considered the outcome of a consultation on a proposal to
amalgamate Nevill Road Infant School and Nevill Road Junior School,
and has:-
 
(1) Given approval to
the proposal without modification to amalgamate Nevill Road Infant
School and Nevill Road Junior School to form a single two-form
entry maintained Nevill Road Primary School for children aged 2 to
11 years. This change would take effect from 1st September 2026,
with a total capacity of 420 and a published admission number (PAN)
of 60, noting with approval that in order
to amalgamate the two schools and create a primary school,
the Council will:
 

·        
close Nevill Road Junior School from 31 August 2026.

·        
expand the age range of Nevill Road Infant School 2 – 11 from
1 September 2026.

·        
change the name of Nevill Road Infant School to Nevill Road Primary
School from 1 September 2026.

·        
enrol all pupils currently on roll at Nevill Road Junior School
into the amalgamated Nevill Road Primary School from 1 September
2026.
 
(2) Agreed to request
that the new governing body consider phasing in any new uniform for
the new Nevill Road Primary School so that parents are not required
to purchase a new uniform unnecessarily.

The alternative option
for Nevill Road Infant School and Nevill Road Junior School is to
do nothing and leave the schools as two separate schools. This
would mean that significant levels of surplus capacity and
predicted budget deficits were not addressed leaving schools in the
area vulnerable to financial instability.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to amalgamate Nevill Road Infant School and Nevill Road Junior School to form a single two-form entry maintained Nevill Road Primary School.

purpose:
This report demonstrates how Stockport Council
is fulfilling its statutory duties required by the Environment Act
2021. This requires public authorities to conserve and enhance
biodiversity and to publish a report outlining achievements and
plans. The report also sets out the council’s biodiversity
targets for the next reporting period, and how progress will be
monitored over the five-year period. The Cabinet will be asked to
note the report.
content:
The Cabinet has
considered the draft Stockport Council Biodiversity Report 2026 and
has:-
 
(1) Approved the
5-year biodiversity plan and corresponding targets, governance and
reporting regime.
 
(2) Approved
publication of the final Biodiversity Report via the
council’s website on or before 26th March 2026 to fulfil the
council’s statutory obligation.

An alternative option
would be to not publish a Biodiversity Report. This would put the
council in breach of our statutory obligation to report every 5
years under Section 40 of the Natural Environment and Rural
Communities Act 2006 (“NERC”) Act, as amended by the
Environment Act 2021. Possible outcomes of this option could result
in reputational damage and an untested sanction from
government.
 
A further alternative
option would be to not manage or enhance biodiversity in the
borough over the next 5 years. This would put us in breach of our
statutory obligation to conserve and protect biodiversity under the
Environment Act 2021. Possible outcomes of this option could result
in reputational damage and an untested sanction from
government.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a 5-year biodiversity plan and publish a Biodiversity Report to fulfill statutory obligations.

purpose:
The Cabinet will be
asked to consider approving the promotion of a compulsory purchase
order to facilitate the assembly of land and property interests to
enable the delivery of attractive public spaces and new public
routes through and between the Stockport 8 regeneration scheme.
content:
The Cabinet will be
asked to consider approving the promotion of a compulsory purchase
order to facilitate the assembly of land and property interests to
enable the delivery of attractive public spaces and new public
routes through and between the Stockport 8 regeneration scheme.

The
Cabinet has considered a report detailing a proposed Compulsory
Purchase Order to enable the delivery of attractive public spaces
and new public routes through and between the Stockport 8
regeneration’ scheme and key destinations and facilities
including the town centre, Stockport Transport Interchange, Viaduct
Park and Stockport train station and has:-
 
(1)
Given approval the preparation and making of a Compulsory Purchase
Order (Order) under section 226(1)(a) of the Town and Country
Planning Act 1990 to facilitate the acquisition of the property
interests in the Arches to facilitate the delivery of attractive
public spaces and key public routes through and between the
Stockport 8 regeneration scheme and key destinations and facilities
including the town centre, Stockport Transport Interchange, Viaduct
Park and Stockport train station;
 
(2)
Delegated authority to the Deputy Chief Executive and the Finance
Director – s151 Officer in consultation with the Cabinet
Member for Economy, Regeneration & Skills authority
to:
 

·        
continue to engage in negotiations and, where
possible, to agree terms for the Council to acquire by voluntary
means all interests in the Arches;

·        
decide if and when to make the Order;
 
(3)
Delegated authority to the Assistant Director for Governance
authority to:
 

·        
take all necessary steps to prepare and make the
Order and supporting documents, including undertaking surveys, and
carrying out a land referencing exercise to check that there are no
property interests in the Arches save for those described
below;

·        
submit the Order to the Secretary of State for
Housing, Communities and Local Government for
confirmation;

·        
if authorised by the Secretary of State, to confirm
the Order;

·        
in the event that objections are made to the Order,
take all necessary steps to address and, where possible, resolve
those objections and, if necessary, to prepare for and participate
in any public inquiry convened by the Secretary of State to
consider the Order;

·        
provided the Order is confirmed by the Secretary of
State (or by the Council as the case may be), take all necessary
steps to exercise powers pursuant to the Order to achieve vacant
possession of the Arches (including the making and service of one
or more General Vesting Declarations and/or the preparation and
service of Notices to Treat and Notices of Entry);

·        
approve agreements with the relevant parties setting
out the terms of the acquisition of the required property interests
and the withdrawals of objections to the Order, together with any
associated or consequential provisions including proposing
modifications to the Order;

·        
participate in any third party proceedings
challenging the confirmation of the Order by the Secretary of State
and/or the exercise of the powers by the Council;

·        
commence or defend proceedings in the Upper Tribunal
(Lands Chamber) concerning the determination of the compensation to
which affected parties whose land and/or interests are acquired
pursuant to the Order may be entitled, and to take all necessary
steps to deal with, settle and/or dispose of those proceedings (as
the case may be).

·        
do all things necessary or incidental to the
implementation of the above-mentioned resolutions.
 
(NOTE:
An appendix to the report contained information ‘Not for
Publication’ that had been circulated to members of the
Cabinet only).

Not to proceed with
making the compulsory purchase order. If the Order is not made, the
Council may be unable to acquire the property interests needed to
deliver important public routes through and between the Stockport 8
regeneration scheme and key destinations and facilities around
Stockport town centre.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a Compulsory Purchase Order to facilitate the delivery of public spaces and routes for the Stockport 8 regeneration scheme.

purpose:
Report to update on the funding and delivery
programme to temporarily relocate the operational bus depot to
enable Phase 1 of Stockport 8 to start on site and to secure
approval to enter into a delivery funding agreement with Greater
Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA)
content:
The Cabinet has
considered a report detailing the funding and delivery programme to
temporarily relocate the operational bus depot to enable Phase 1 of
Stockport 8 to start on site and has then agree that:-
 
(1) Subject to TfGM
securing approval from the BNC, approve the Council entering into a
funding agreement with GMCA as outlined in this report and using
the funding to deliver the temporary bus depot.
 
(2)  Authority be delegated to the Deputy Chief
Executive and the Director of Finance - Section 151 Officer, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Economy, Regeneration
& Skills to finalise the terms of the supporting legal
agreements outlined in the report and Confidential Appendix 2 along
with any other ancillary agreements and formally enter into the
documentation required to give effect to those such terms;
 
(3) Authority be
delegated to the Assistant Director – Governance to do all
things necessary or incidental to the implementation of the
above-mentioned resolutions.
 
(NOTE: An appendix to
the report contained information ‘Not for Publication’
that had been circulated to members of the Cabinet only).

Not to enter into a
delivery funding agreement or deliver a temporary bus depot. This
would delay the delivery of Stockport 8 Phase 1 until a permanent
new facility is secured and delivered by TfGM, anticipated in
2029/30. Delay to the delivery of Phase 1 would result in
substantial inflationary cost pressure potentially rendering the
scheme unviable and would place the £41.3m GMCA Good Growth
funding secured at risk. Delay and the implications to scheme
viability would also impact the repayment profile of the
Council’s investment to date into Stockport 8.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve funding for the temporary relocation of the operational bus depot to enable Phase 1 of Stockport 8 to start on site.

purpose:
The Pay Policy Statement sets out the
Council’s approach to pay policy in accordance with the
requirements of Section 38 of the Localism Act 2011. The statement
also has due regard for the associated statutory guidance including
supplementary guidance issued in February 2013 and the Local
Government Transparency code 2014. The statement also incorporates
the Council’s Gender Pay Gap (GPG) information in order to
fulfil the Council’s obligation to publish this on an annual
basis under the GPG reporting requirements.


The purpose of the statement is to provide transparency with regard
to the Council’s approach to setting the pay of its employees
(excluding teaching staff working in local authority schools) by
confirming the methods by which salaries of Council employees are
determined; the detail and level of remuneration of its most senior
staff i.e. ‘chief officers’, as defined by the relevant
legislation; the responsibility of the Appointments Committee to
ensure the provisions set out in this statement relating to the
Chief
Executive, Deputy Chief Executive, Executive Directors and
Directors are applied consistently throughout the Council and
recommend any amendments to the Council.

content:
A representative of
the Assistant Director for Governance submitted a report of the
Director of Place Management (copies of which had been circulated)
setting out a request for the allocation of ward budget for site
security works at Woodsmoor Playing
Field and Chester Road Playing Field.
 
The following comments
were made/ issues raised:
 

·        
Members and officers had been working to find solutions to secure
local playing field sites and prevent further unauthorised
incursions.

·        
The proposal for Woodsmore Playing
Field involved the installation of a heavy duty swing barrier to
improve site security.

·        
The proposal for the Chester Road playing field included improved
security works to prevent incursions.

·        
There had been a recent spate of incursions on those playing
fields.

·        
It was acknowledged that no measure could be 100 per cent effective
however, barriers slowed down incursions and enabled residents to
report promptly suspicious activity to the police.

·        
The barriers bought valuable time for the police and council to
respond to incursions.

·        
Members referred to a recent incident at Chester Road where noise
from removing a barrier had alerted residents and police, allowing
the incursion to be prevented early; travellers had been unable to
occupy the site for more than a brief period.

·        
There had been significant damage to property resulting from past
incursions, such as that which had occurred at the Stockport
Georgians Cricket Club.

·        
During that incursion safety concerns had included rocks being
thrown at young girls playing cricket. Furthermore, the site had
been left in an extremely poor conditions, requiring officers to
clear large amounts of human waste. Officers were thanked for their
difficult work in restoring sites following incursions.

·        
During previous incursions at Chester Road, the use of heavy logs
as barriers had proved to be inadequate.

·        
Furthermore, there had been disruption and vandalism including
damage to the Norbury Lacrosse Club and its changing rooms, paint
vandalism and damage at Woodsmore
affecting the cricket club.

·        
Members highlighted the financial cost and resource burden of
repairing damage.
 
RESOLVED – (1)
That the Cabinet Member for Finance and Resource be recommended to
give approval to a new heavy duty swing barrier to improve site
security at Woodsmoor Playing Field at
a cost of £3,000 with £1,150 to be funded from the Ward
Discretionary Budget (Norbury and Woodsmoor ward allocation) and £1,850 to be
funded from the Ward Delegated Budget (Norbury and Woodsmoor ward allocation).
 
(2) That approval be
given to the costs of improved site security works at Chester Road
Playing Field at a cost of £6,500 to be funded from the Ward
Delegated Budget (Norbury and Woodsmoor
ward allocation).

content:
The Director of Finance (S151 Officer) in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Finance & Resources has given approval to
the:-

(1) Implementing the Government’s 15% business rates relief
for pubs and live music venues and Supporting Small Business Relief
for 2026-27 in accordance with the eligibility criteria and
guidance issued by HM Treasury and the Department for Levelling Up,
Housing and Communities.

(2) Applying the relief strictly in line with the
Government’s prescribed definitions and policy intent,
exercising local discretion only where eligibility is unclear and
where doing so remains consistent with national guidance.

(3) The amendments made to the Council's Business Rates
Discretionary Relief Policy at paragraphs 2.5, 2.6 and the addition
of Sections 15 and 16, to reflect the introduction of these
reliefs.

The Director of Finance noted that the relief will be administered
using existing business rates processes, with any loss of income to
be compensated through Government grant funding arrangements.

The context to this decision is based on HM Treasury announcing a
new package of business rates support for 2026–27 including
relief for pubs and live music venues along with supporting small
business relief. The relief will be delivered using the
Council’s discretionary powers under Section 47 of the Local
Government Finance Act 1988. While local authorities must adopt a
discretionary scheme, the Government requires that awards be made
in accordance with national criteria.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Parks, Highways & Transport Services
content:
The
Cabinet Member for Parks, Highways & Transport Services has
considered a proposal to introduce carriageway and footway widening
along the section of Marple Road between its junctions with
Offerton Road and Dooley Lane and has given approval to the
proposed scheme as detailed in the report and the main features of
which are described below, to be funded from the City Region
Sustainable Transport Settlement (CRSTS):-
 

Widening of Marple Road, to facilitate extended left turn lanes on
Marple Road at the junctions with Offerton Road and Dooley Lane to
improve the operation of the junctions. The left turn lane to
Offerton Road would be extended by 25m and that to Dooley Lane by
44m. This would reduce incidences where vehicles in the single lane
part of the queue cannot access the left turn filter due to the
ahead movement queue and so improve junction efficiency.The
eastbound bus stop would be relocated to reflect the revised
kerbline, with provision of a raised kerb to allow for level access
to and from the buses.
Widening of the pavement along the same length as the carriageway
is being widened with a length of 95m widened to 2m in width.The
proposals require 15 trees to be removed, of varying sizes, which
are covered by a TPO. Some of the trees are showing signs of
dieback as
mentioned in Appendix B and the trees removed would be replaced in
the
vicinity. Should the scheme be approved, a comprehensive
Arboriculture and Ecology report would be commissioned to inform an
application for the trees to be removed.

An alternative scheme layout which provided
for the extension to the left turn lanes on Marple Road, at the
junctions with Offerton Road and Dooley Lane, and also provided
improved segregated pedestrian and cycle facilities on the northern
side of the carriageway was considered. This proposal would require
the use of a greater area of land which is currently within private
ownership and structural works over Torkington Brook. This option
would significantly exceed the budget available within the Bus
Pinch Points programme and was therefore unable to be progressed.
The
works proposed would not prejudice development of such a scheme in
the future should funding be identified.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Parks, Highways & Transport Services has decided to approve the widening of Marple Road to improve junction efficiency.

(i.e. mandatory 97% pass through rates for early years and minimum
funding levels (MFLs) for schools, etc).
 
In relation to the local schools funding
formula model for primary schools, the local model used is aligned
to a continued phased transition approach towards the national
funding formula (NFF) model to avoid significant turbulence in
individual school funding allocations across the borough.

purpose:
This comprehensive report sets out the
council’s Treasury Management Strategies for 2026/27 which
are constructed in full compliance with the CIPFA Treasury
Management Code and the council's Treasury Management Policy
Statement and Practices.
content:
The Cabinet has
considered the Treasury Management Strategy and Annual Investment
Strategy Mid-Year Review Report 2026/27 and has agreed to
recommended that the Council Meeting approves:-
 
(1) The Minimum
Revenue Provision Policy for 2026/27.
 
(2) The Capital
Expenditure forecasts and Capital Financing Requirement
projections.
 
(3) The Treasury
Management Strategy 2026/27.
 
(4) The Treasury and
Prudential Indicators and limits 2026/27-2028/29; and
 
(5) The Annual
Investment Strategy 2026/27.

When formulating the
2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy, the council undertakes a
comprehensive review of all available treasury options to determine
the optimal, most cost-effective, and least-risk approach to
managing its finances. This involves a meticulous evaluation of
potential actions across the core treasury disciplines. Borrowing
options are assessed to determine the best method for funding
capital expenditure, considering sources such as the Public Works
Loan Board (PWLB), market loans, and prudential borrowing, while
weighing fixed versus variable interest rates and maturity profiles
to mitigate refinancing risk.
 
Concurrently, all
appropriate investment avenues are considered to manage surplus
cash balances, ranging from secure, highly liquid options like
money market funds and other local authorities to term deposits
with approved high-credit-quality banking counterparties, always
prioritising security and liquidity over yield in line with the
Annual Investment Strategy. The strategy formulation process
synthesises these variables, including current economic commentary
and interest rate forecasts, to create a coherent plan that
balances risk, cost, and statutory requirements

purpose:
The Cabinet will be asked to consider the
proposed admission arrangements for Stockport junior community
junior schools and proposed changes to the Published Admission
Numbers at Nevill Road Infant School and Nevill Road Junior School
for admission in September 2027. The report makes recommendations
to the Cabinet following a public consultation on the proposals.
The admission arrangements in effect for September 2026 for
Stockport community and voluntary controlled infant, primary and
secondary schools will remain largely the same for September 2027
apart from points of clarification recommended by the School
Adjudicator.
content:
The Cabinet has
considered a report outlining the recent consultation on amendments
to the admission arrangements for junior schools in Stockport for
which Stockport Council is the admission authority and the
published admission numbers at Nevill Road Infant School and Nevill
Road Junior School for September 2027, and has:-
 
(1) Approved that the
admission arrangements for Stockport maintained community and
voluntary controlled schools are determined for September 2027 as
set out in Appendix 1.
 
(2) Approved the
reduction of the published admission number at Nevill Road Infant
School to 60 from September 2027
 
(3) Approved the
reduction of the published admission number at Nevill Road Junior
School to 60 from September 2027
 
(4) Delegated the
decision to proceed to the publication of statutory proposals to
the Director of Education, Work and Skills in consultation with
Cabinet Member for Children, Families and Education having
considered the outcome of the initial consultation.
 
(5) Noted the outcome
of the Integrated Impact Assessment. 
The IIA notes that the reduction in the proposed Published
Admission Numbers at Nevill Road Infant School and Nevill Road
Junior School has some positive and negative short-term
impacts.  The schools affected
are able to access support from
Stockport Council if the reduction means that staffing at the
schools needs to be reduced.  It also
allows for an improvement in the local environment as temporary
accommodation that is reaching the end of its useful life can be
removed.

The alternative option
for Nevill Road Infant School and Nevill Road Junior School is to
do nothing and leave the Published Admission Numbers as they are.
This would mean that significant levels of surplus capacity were
not addressed leaving schools in the area vulnerable to financial
instability. It would also mean that accommodation that almost
reached the end of its useful life cannot be addressed.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve amendments to the admission arrangements for junior schools in Stockport, including a reduction in admission numbers at Nevill Road Infant School and Nevill Road Junior School for September 2027.

Arthur Street – (Southern / Eastern / Northern Sides)

From a point 29.5
metres west of the intersection of the western kerbline of Margaret Street for a distance of 2 metres in a westerly direction, then

will include:
 

·      
Widening of the existing Arthur Street path to create a 3m wide
shared-use footway cycleway.

·      
Relocation of lighting columns to the side of the Arthur Street
path.

·      
Provision of a new intersecting 3m shared-use path across the verge
connecting Bedford Street (to the north) with Bedford Street (to
the south).

·      
Provision of shared use signage, bollards and dropped kerbs at the
ends of the path.

·      
Provision of double yellow lines to prevent vehicles from blocking
the dropped kerbs.

·      
Two trees would need to be removed to accommodate the works. These
would be replaced within the vicinity.

None.

None.

purpose:
This report deals with the forecast Collection
Fund outturn position for 2025/26, the setting of the Council Tax
Taxbase for 2026/27 and also presents a forecast for Business Rates
income expected in 2026/27.These items form an integral and
important part of the Council’s budget setting and MTFP
process
content:
The Cabinet considered
the forecast Collection Fund outturn position for 2025/26, the
setting of the Council Tax Taxbase for 2026/27, and a forecast for
Business Rates income for 2026/27 and agreed:-
 
(1) That the
Cabinet:-
 

(i)           
Declare a provisional forecast outturn Collection Fund deficit to
be appropriated to the council’s General Fund in 2026/27 of
£0.754m relating to a Council Tax deficit of £0.810m
and Business Rates surplus of £0.056m subject to the
delegations below.
 

(ii)         
Note the proposal for the Council Tax Discretionary Hardship Fund
as set out in the Council Tax and Business Rates Discounts Annual
Review report as per paragraph 3.5
 

(iii)        
Note the 2026/27 Council Tax Taxbase for budget setting purposes of
99,698.1 Band D equivalent dwellings. The council’s final
2026/27 Council Tax Taxbase will be presented for approval to the
council meeting on 15 January 2026
 

(iv)        
Note that the indicative Collection Fund resources identified are
to be reviewed through the MTFP and 2026/27 budget setting
processes following the Provisional Local Government Finance
Settlement in December.
 
(2) That the following
decisions be delegated to the Director of Finance (Section 151
Officer) in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Finance &
Resources:-
 

(i)           
The decision to change the provisional 2025/26 Collection Fund
forecast outturn position prior to declaring the position on 31
January 2026 as required by legislation.

 

(ii)         
The decision to change the Business Rates forecast linked to the
submission of the NNDR1 (Business Rates budget) to Government;
and
 

(iii)        
The decision to decline the Greater Manchester Business Rates
pooling arrangement.

None.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to declare a provisional forecast outturn Collection Fund deficit for 2026/27.

purpose:
The Cabinet is asked
to agree the terms outlined in the proposed School Investment Plan
and the associated investment detailed in the Education Asset
Management Plan.
content:
The Cabinet is asked
to agree the terms outlined in the proposed School Investment Plan
and the associated investment detailed in the Education Asset
Management Plan.

The Cabinet has
considered a report detailing a proposed School Investment Plan and
Education Asset Management Plan, and has:-
 
(1) Agreed the terms
outlined in the School Investment Plan and approve the programme of
works set out in the Education Asset Management Plan (Appendix 1)
for inclusion in the 2026/27 financial year.
 
(2) Delegated
authority to the Assistant Director of Estates and Asset
Management, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for finance and
resources, and a majority of members of the LA’s Capital
Board to procure the works and services and subsequently determine
the outcome of any contract award process for any project specified
in the asset management plan.
 
(3) Delegated
authority to the Director of Education, Work and Skills and
Assistant Director of Estate and Asset Management, in consultation
with the Cabinet Member for Finance and Resources, and a majority
of members of the LA’s Capital Board, to recycle any unspent
School Condition Allocation (SCA ) funding back into the Capital
Programme, which in turn can address any unforeseen issues and / or
required schemes that not listed within the 2026/27 asset
management plan due to funding constraints.
 
(4) Delegated
authority to the Director of Education, Work, and Skills in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Children, Families and
Education, to determine, allocate, and deploy capital funding to
projects, schools, or trusts to create additional mainstream,
resource base, special school places.
 
(5) Delegated
authority to the Director for Education, Work, and Skills and the
Assistant Director of Governance in consultation with the Cabinet
Member for Children, Families and Education, to finalise terms and
enter into funding agreements as necessary with schools and trusts
that are linked to the investment and creation of new school
places.

None.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the School Investment Plan and Education Asset Management Plan for the 2026/27 financial year.

purpose:
This report provides Cabinet with a mid-year
review of the council’s Treasury Management Strategy
Statement and Annual Investment Strategy for 2025/26, approved by
council on 27 February 2025, and has been prepared in accordance
with the Chartered Institute of Public Finance Accountancy (CIPFA)
Code of Practice for Treasury Management in the Public Services.
The report also consults the Corporate, Resource Management and
Governance (CRMG) Scrutiny Committee on the development of the
council’s Treasury Management Strategy Statement (TMSS),
Annual Investment Strategy (AIS) and Minimum Revenue Provision
(MRP) Policy for 2026/27, to be considered for approval at the
Cabinet Meeting on 10 February 2026 and the Council Meeting on 26
February 2026
content:
The Cabinet has
considered the Treasury Management Strategy and Annual Investment
Strategy Mid-Year Review Report 2025/26 and has agreed to
recommended that the Council Meeting:-
 
(1) Note the report
and the treasury activity in the first half of the financial
year.
 
(2) Approve and note
the Treasury Management Strategy, Annual Investment Strategy and
Minimum Revenue Provision Policy for 2025/26 approved in February
2025, will continue to be followed considering the forecasts and
conclusions set out in the report.
 
(3) Note the revised
interest rate forecasts for Bank Rate and PWLB rates over the short
and medium-term, which will drive the council’s long-term
borrowing strategies going forward.
 
(4) Note the amendment
to the council’s MRP Policy, which has come about due to the
mandatory adoption of IFRS16 Leases accounting standard for the
2024/25 Statement of Accounts.
 
(5) Consider the
statements with regard to the Treasury Strategy for 2026/27.

None.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Treasury Management Strategy and Annual Investment Strategy Mid-Year Review Report 2025/26.

purpose:
Details about the implementation of
Biodiversity Net Gain legislation at the council, including the
creation of a habitat banking vehicle for the provision of
biodiversity units on council-owned land to fulfil demand for
developments that require offsite biodiversity
enhancement.
content:
The Cabinet has
considered a report detailing a proposal to create and sell
Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) units on Council owned land, working in
conjunction with Greater Manchester Combined Authority who would
offer the necessary ‘Responsible Body’ function to
facilitate the BNG service, and has:-
 
(1) Given approval in
principle to the proposal to utilise the ‘Responsible
Body’ route offered by the GMCA for the purpose of creating
and selling Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) units on Council owned
land.
 
(2) Delegated
authority to Deputy Chief Executive, in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Housing & Environment, to finalise the terms
of the agreement with the GMCA or to adopt alternative arrangements
for the discharge of the Council’s duty to develop and sell
BNG units in the light of prevailing circumstances.
 
(3) Given approval in
principle to the selection and designation of three sites proposed
for habitat bank creation as detailed in Section 8 of the
report.
 
(4) Delegated
authority to the Director of Place Management, in consultation with
the Cabinet Member for Housing & Environment, to finalise the
designation and delivery of the sites selected for habitat bank
creation; or the selection, designation and approval of alternative
suitable council owned sites to deliver BNG units should those
identified in Section 8 of the report not prove viable.
 
(5) Delegated
authority to authority to the Director of Place Management, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Housing & Environment,
to determine when it may be viable to proceed with creating BNG
units on council owned land, following financial and legal
appraisal.

None.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to create and sell Biodiversity Net Gain units on Council owned land in partnership with Greater Manchester Combined Authority.

purpose:
Consideration of the discounts and support
available in respect of Business Rates and Council Tax for the Year
2026/27
content:
The Cabinet has
considered proposed changes to the scheme of local discounts and
exemptions against liability for Business Rates and Council Tax and
has agreed:-
 
(1) That the
discretionary reliefs outlined in the Business Rates Discretionary
Relief Policy (Appendix 1) be retained for 2026–27. In
addition, the Policy will no longer include reference to Large
Investors, as such cases will now be considered under the
Exceptional Circumstances provision.
 
(2) That the amendment
to the Business Rates Discretionary Relief Policy at point 1.5
(Appendix 1) is endorsed, to ensure discretionary support is not
used to offset the impact of changes in national government
policy.
 
(3) That the council
continues with its existing empty property discount and premium
scheme as shown in the table at 4.2.1 for 2026-27.
 
(4) That exceptions to
both the long-term empty property premium and the second home
premium be limited to those required by legislation, as outlined in
sections 4.3.2 and 4.3.3, and applied in accordance with published
statutory guidance.
 
(6) That the Council
Tax Empty Homes Policy (Appendix 2), which sets out
Stockport’s approach to charging Council Tax on unoccupied
properties within the borough is approved.
 
(7) That any Council
Tax liability for care leavers up to the age of 25 continues to be
reduced to zero for 2026-27.
 
(8) That
Stockport’s Council Tax Support scheme is maintained for
2026-27 as detailed at Appendix 3.
 
(9) That the Council
Tax discretionary fund is set at £0.1m for 2026-27,
supporting customers facing financial difficulty, with no
alternative means. 
 
(10) That delegation
is given to the Director of Finance in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Finance and Resources to review and adjust the
fund during 2026-27, capped at a total of £0.15m if required,
to support the council’s ongoing cost-of-living response.
 
(11) That delegation
is given to the Director of Finance (Section 151 Officer) in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Finance and Resources to
consider any subsequent Government announcements that impact on
Business Rates and Council Tax reductions for 2026-27, and to
decide what changes should be made aligned to legislation.

None.

None.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to make changes to local discounts and exemptions for Business Rates and Council Tax for the upcoming year.

purpose:
To meet statutory requirements set out in the
Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 (as amended) the council,
as Local Planning Authority, has to prepare and maintain an
up-to-date local plan.

The purpose of the report is to set out details relating to the
emerging draft Stockport Local Plan and seek Cabinet agreement that
it be subject to a period of public consultation commencing on 6th
November 2025 and continuing until 21st December 2025.
content:
The Cabinet has
considered a report detailing the emerging draft Stockport Local
Plan that has been developed in order to meet statutory
requirements as set out in the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act
2004 (as amended) that requires the council, as Local Planning
Authority, to prepare and maintain an up-to-date local plan and
that it be subject to a period of public consultation commencing on
6th November 2025 and continuing until 21st December 2025, and
has:-
 
(1) Given approval for
consultation between 6 November 2025 and 21 December 2025 the
emerging draft Local Plan as set out in Appendix 1 of the main
report and draft updated policies map as set out in Appendix 2 of
the main report which will take place under Regulation 18 of the
Town and Country Planning (Local Planning) (England) Regulations
2012 and be carried out in accordance with the council’s
adopted Statement of Community Involvement.
 
(2) Delegated the
making of minor amendments to the emerging draft Local Plan and/or
the draft updated policies map prior to the consultation commencing
to the Assistant Director Place Making and Planning in consultation
with the Leader of the Council and the Cabinet Member for Housing
and Environment. Minor amendments might include, for instance,
correcting typographical errors or updating references/links to
supporting evidence documents.

None.

None.

content:
The Director of
Education, Work & Skills has considered a report outlining work
undertaken at a Greater Manchester level in relation to post 16
travel assistance and detailing a revised Post-16 policy which
seeks to place greater reliance on community travel arrangements,
independent travel training and the use of personal
budget.  In doing so, there are a range
of key policy and practice changes that require public consultation
before a final decision can be made. An equalities impact
assessment will accompany any proposals once consultation has taken
place.

The Director of Education, Work & Skills, in consultation with
the Cabinet Member for Children, Families & Education, has then
given approval to proceed to a public consultation in respect of
the revised Post-16 policy that will be published on 3 November
2025 and closing 8 December 2025 which proposes changes to the
transport policy which would align our local post-16 policy to the
GM policy and propose to seek best value from all and new private
hire contracts the LA enters into in relation to School Transport,
and explore how this can be done with stakeholders in the private
hire market.

None.
topline: The Director of Education, Work & Skills has decided to revise the Post-16 travel assistance policy for public consultation.
